newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Metro Pacific Q1 net seen sustainable.
newsitem.headline: Metro Pacific Q1 net seen sustainable.

text.p: Metro Pacific Corp's (MPC) strong performance in the first quarter of 1997 was an impressive start to the year and the company was expected to maintain the momentum, analysts said on Friday.

Metro Pacific, the Philippine arm of First Pacific Co Ltd, said earlier on Friday its net income soared to 200.513 million pesos in the first quarter compared to 90.476 million in the same period last year.
"Profit before other income grew from 98 million pesos in (the first quarter) of 1996 to 150 million," this year, MPC said.
"The first quarter figures are an impressive start for MPC," said Jomar Lacson, analyst at Philippine Asia Equity Securities Inc.

Reuben Hermoso, analyst at Dharmala Securities Phils Inc, said he expected the firm to sustain its strong growth for the rest of the year due to the "rising number of subscribers of Smart Communications Inc and the Fort Bonifacio project."

Equity in net earnings of affiliated companies of MPC rose by 289 percent to 195 million pesos from 50 million due to the group's interests in property development and telecommunications, MPC said in a statement.
"For the first quarter of 1997, MPC has once again reported a significant growth in net income, and this creates a sound base for the rest of the year," president Napoleon Nazareno said.

"The substantial increase in the group's recurring income has been achieved through planned strategic investments over recent years in rapidly developing sectors allowing MPC to create sustainable platform for growth," he added.

MPC unit Fort Bonifacio Development Corp, which is developing a 214-hectare property on the edge of Manila's Makati commercial district, reported a significant increase in net income in the first quarter.
"...Certain buyers paid fully for their lots in Fort Bonifacio and thereby obtained title to the land," MPC said.
Traders said they expected MPC to book more earnings for the rest of the year on reports that Fort Bonifacio Development had made advance lot sales worth a total of 29 billion pesos.

"The Fort Bonifacio project will be a main revenue earner for MPC since buyers of the lots will make payments on the property in the next 10 years," said Raul Ruiz, reseach director at Sun Hung Kai Securities.
Smart, another revenue earner of MPC this year, is expected to double its subscriber base by the end of the year from 383,000 as of end of March, Dharmala's Hermoso said.
"The prudent approach in the management of Smart's financial affairs has enabled it to maintain tight control over its accounts receivable and fraud has been substantially avoided," MPC said.
Smart plans to make an initial public offering in the third quarter of the year.
Asia Equity's Lacson said he expected Steniel Manufacturing Corp, MPC's packaging unit, to break-even in 1997 while Dharmala's Hermoso expected the firm to post profits of 17 million pesos.
Steniel had reported a 245.6 million pesos net loss in 1996.
